posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
@EdenTheBard
a Photograph of your monitor is not the same as a screenshot.
to make a screenshot, press [alt]-[prtscrn] on your keyboard, then open paint and press [ctrl]-[v] for paste
additionally, an event is more than its content area - the properties on the left side and the page numbers above are as important for more complex events.
So when asking for screenshots we usually want the full event window, not only the right half of it.
As for your problem, don't use the game over command. That event command is made to be the end of your game, preventing any continuation.
a better way would be to only pretend to be a game over by using show picture for the game over picture and whatever you want to happen then.
or use a plugin for something called "new game plus", although that is usually meant for continuing after winning the game. But it can easiyl be used in your way.

posts.body:
EdenTheBard said:
How do I do that?
Click to expand...
The Change Save Access event command on the third tab of event commands. Disabling it disables the autosave, then you can turn it back on after the battle processing command in your event.
EdenTheBard said:
how am I supposed to like remind people to save frequently without it disrupting?

Why would you? People have been saving their games for decades without needing any kind of constant reminder.
It's hard to read a camera photo of your monitor, and it's honestly kind of a silly thing to do when there are numerous ways built into your operating system to take a screenshot and just paste it into your post
Here's an instructional article that comes up when I Google it:
7 Easy Methods for Taking Screenshots in Windows 11 - CNET
When you need to take a screenshot in Windows 11, you've got options.

posts.author: Kes
posts.body:
We were all beginners once, and all had to learn how to get help solving our problems.
In short, we had to learn how to help other people help us.
The most basic way is to give the needed information in the way that's most useful for detecting the cause of the problem.  A key component of that info is an adequate screenshot.  No matter how lazy you're feeling (and we all feel lazy sometimes), it's really a non-negotiable.

As I explained in my answer earlier in this topic, your photo was missing important parts of the event.

additionally you found out yourself that photos are usually very big pictures due to the high resolution of cameras.
